question: A rectangular garden \(50\) feet long and \(10\) feet wide is enclosed by a fence. To make the garden larger, while using the same fence, its shape is changed to a square. By how many square feet does this enlarge the garden?
solution:
Using the same fence keeps the perimeter unchanged. The rectangle's perimeter is
\[
2(50+10)=120\text{ feet}.
\]
A square has four equal sides, so each new side is \(120\div4=30\) feet. The original area is \(50\cdot10=500\) square feet, and the new area is \(30\cdot30=900\) square feet. Thus the garden grows by
\[
900-500=\boxed{400\text{ square feet}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
